# Introduction {.smaller}

::: columns
::: {.column width=75%}

Critical Role is a weekly web series of a group of voice actors who play Dungeons & Dragons 
[@wiki; @critrole].

- 4 main campaigns (or seasons)
- \> 1000 hours of screen time
- Kickstarter:
  - The Legend of Vox Machina (based on Campaign 1)
  - The Mighty Nein (based on Campaign 2)
- Etc.
- More info...

# Data {.smaller}

All plots and tables on the following slides were created using the following datasets. 

```{r data show}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

data <- read_csv("data/criticalrole.csv", show_col_types = F)
info <- read_csv("data/info.csv", show_col_types = F)

```

## Campaigns {.smaller}
This interactive plot gives an overview of the number of episodes and the amount of hours per
campaign (or season). Note that Campaign 4 is ongoing.

```{r plot}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

p <- info |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Episodes", "Runtime"), names_to = "type", values_to = "value") |> 
  mutate(text = case_when(type == "Episodes" ~ paste0("Number of episodes: ", value),
                          type == "Runtime"  ~ paste0("Runtime: ", value, " hours")),
         type = case_when(type == "Episodes" ~ "Number of episodes",
                          type == "Runtime" ~ "Runtime (in hours)")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(Campaign, value, fill = type, text = text)) + 
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    labs(y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() + 
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),
          panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray60", linewidth = 0.4),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#B66353FF", "#A2CEAAFF")) 

ggplotly(p, tooltip = c("Campaign", "text"))

```


## My data {.smaller}
I have previously gathered my own watch history data on Critical Role and have calculated 
the number of episodes and amount of hours I watched per day for each campaign.

```{r table}
#| echo: false
#| layout-ncol: 1
#| height: auto

data |> 
  mutate(days = as.numeric(as.Date(end, format = "%d/%m/%Y") - 
                             as.Date(start, format = "%d/%m/%Y") + 1),
         `episodes per day` = round(episodes / as.numeric(days), 2),
         `hours per day` = round(runtime / as.numeric(days), 2)) |> 
  select(campaign, start, end, days, `episodes per day`, `hours per day`) |> 
  datatable(class = c("stripe", "hover"),
            rownames = F,
            colnames = c("Campaign", "Start date", "End date", "Days", "Episodes (per day)", 
                         "Hours (per day)"),
            options = list(dom = 't',
                           columnDefs = list(
                             list(className = "dt-right", width = "10%", targets = 0),
                             list(className = "dt-center", width = "20%", targets = 1:2),
                             list(className = "dt-center", width = "10%", targets = 3),
                             list(className = "dt-center", width = "20%", targets = 4:5)
                           )))

```

## Critical Role 24/7 {.smaller}

If you did not eat or sleep, it would take $x$ days to watch all available episodes of Critical
Role's main campaigns.

## Critical Role 24/7 {.smaller}
If you did not eat or sleep, it would take $x$ days to watch all available episodes of Critical
Role's main campaigns.

\begin{aligned}

x &= \frac{453 + 566 + 508 + 148}{24} \\
  &= \frac{1675}{24} \\
  &= 69.79167 \\
  &\approx 70

\end{aligned}

It would take nearly 70 days, or 10 weeks.
